newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: High China diesel stocks pressure domestic prices.
newsitem.headline: High China diesel stocks pressure domestic prices.

text.p: High diesel stocks in China and Hong Kong could force state-refiner SINOPEC to lower wholesale prices sold from its refineries, Chinese traders said on Thursday.
"They (SINOPEC) want to lower it by 100 yuan because more import cargoes are coming in at lower prices and it would make domestic diesel uncompetitive," a trader with a Chinese trading company said.
Current ex-refinery diesel price is 2,190 yuan per tonne, compared to ex-ship offers by some foreign trading firms at around 1,850 yuan.
Traders said SINOPEC has been trying to reduce ex-refinery diesel price over the past two months, especially when crude prices hit a low in April.
But the current high stockpile and low international prices would make this more urgent, they said.
If ex-refinery prices were lowered, SINOPEC would make it a point that state importers limit their imports, they added.

Traders said the brimming stocks were due to large imports during April resulting in ships lining up to discharge at the southern Chinese port of Xiamen. They said there are currently an estimated eleven 30,000-tonnes vessels waiting offshore.
Smuggling activities and Chinese refineries returning from scheduled maintenance turnarounds have worsened the situation, traders said.
They said the central government would further tighten its grip on fuel smuggling as this remained a problem despite a recent clampdown which saw more patrols in the southern ports.
Traders said regional diesel prices are also under pressure due to plentiful stocks still unsold from the recent influx of arbitrage cargoes from the West - totalling about three million tonnes.
Singapore trader Hin Leong took at last half of that, with some being sold to India and other regional endusers, but large volumes remained unsold with about seven sellers still seeking buyers.

Traders said at least two ships have been diverted to Hong Kong. Despite reports of sales into the British colony, refiners with storage terminals said they would be hard pressed to accept more cargoes as their tanks are also full.
"There is no room in the Hong Kong storage," a trader with a US refiner said. "We would love to have the cargoes but there is absolutely no space."

The refiner who recently bought a 30,000-tonne parcel from a South Korean refiner at $1.05 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight Hong Kong, said premiums now have to be below $1.00 to attract buyers.

Traders said this, as well as the return of refineries from maintenance shutdown, have forced up Singapore middle-distillate stocks to an at least three-year record of 10.35 million barrels for the week ended May 21.
Barely two months ago, stocks plunged to an at least three-year low of 4.95 million barrels.
The abundant supplies would put additional pressure on regional diesel values which have been getting strong support at the $25.00-per-barrel mark, they said.

Swaps diesel price for June lost 20 cents late on Thursday to be last quoted at $25.20/$25.30, and traders said the softer tone were reflected on the physical market. Late Thursday, physical trades were seen at $25.10 and $25.20 a barrel down 15-25 cents from Tuesday.
-- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
